strategic_horizon.terminal_goal: Build a personal weak-network VPN whose two primary transport properties are UDP/datagram-like earliest-complete inner delivery and TCP-shaped FakeTCP outer behavior. Current release qualification assumes at most a 100 Mbit/s weak public link. The personal server uses one shared username/password for many concurrent sessions, OpenWrt final capture is TPROXY, and Windows final capture is TUN/Wintun-class.
strategic_horizon.current_milestone: Finish the 100 Mbit/s transport gates and shared-account session plumbing without changing already-qualified no-HOL semantics, then freeze the protocol before final OpenWrt TPROXY and Windows TUN integration.
strategic_horizon.local_optimization_stop_rule: Inner first-complete latency and delivery are the first optimization priority. Do not delay an available systematic source, do not make inner delivery wait for cumulative TCP ACK/retransmission, do not add authentication/control complexity that is unnecessary for the personal shared-account deployment, and do not let platform capture requirements change the frozen transport protocol.

continuation_cursor.last_completed_action: Changed the active product assumptions to a 100 Mbit/s weak-link ceiling, simple shared username/password admission, and final platform targets OpenWrt TPROXY plus Windows TUN. Added a same-entry Reality-like simple auth path that sends one bounded username/password request inside TLS 1.3 and immediately issues a fresh one-time 32-byte ticket; the same credentials can issue multiple concurrent independent tickets. Added a session registry keyed by 32-byte live session ID rather than username. GitHub Actions demo-encryption run 32891427104 passed the simplified path end-to-end with an unrelated self-signed front certificate, verify_server=false, DTLS verify=none, ticket bind with auth=false, encrypted echo, and pcap scan showing no username/password/ticket/WBDC/application plaintext. Converted active FakeTCP first-arrival, full-stack first-arrival and recovery A/B qdiscs to 100mbit. Added a loaded recovery A/B with 65 Mbit/s inner offered traffic on a 100 Mbit/s link at RTT 20/100 ms and loss 10/20%. Added OpenWrt TPROXY render/apply/cleanup plumbing with underlay escape before capture and compact nft sets, plus contract tests. Updated the constitution, ADR-0008, ROADMAP and handoff architecture tests so old per-device credential and mandatory certificate/hostname-validation requirements no longer define the personal product.
continuation_cursor.current_task: Get the current 100 Mbit/s regression set green and use the loaded legacy-vs-SACK/RACK result to make the recovery default decision. In parallel, preserve the deliberately simple one-account/many-session model and prepare the server data-plane demultiplexing boundary without introducing username-keyed live state or a multi-tenant control plane.
continuation_cursor.why_now: Low-load same-binary recovery A/B already showed SACK/RACK adds only roughly 0.00-0.055 ms p50/p75 body latency while raising five-second delivery by about 7-19 percentage points, but that test was only around 9.6 Mbit/s. The user capped the real weak link at 100 Mbit/s, so loaded behavior near that capacity is the remaining transport decision. Authentication simplification and Reality-like ticket join have already passed a real encrypted end-to-end CI demo, so the next correctness gap is concurrent data-session ownership rather than more identity machinery.
continuation_cursor.done_when: The loaded 100 Mbit/s recovery A/B either passes its p50/goodput gates and SACK/RACK remains default, or it fails and advanced recovery is demoted/refactored so new inner datagrams keep priority. Current go test/handoff tests and the 100 Mbit/s first-arrival/full-stack regressions are green. Same shared username/password can create multiple distinct tickets and live server state remains keyed by session/ticket identity. Only after these protocol gates are frozen should OpenWrt TPROXY and Windows TUN be connected to the real data session and each platform run one clean end-to-end VPN success with underlay escape and cleanup.
continuation_cursor.next_atomic_action: Poll the current faketcp-recovery-load-ab, ci, fullstack-first-arrival and demo-encryption runs for checkpoint 1b43227de133a675db0017c9803288d04de175c5. If loaded recovery passes, persist SACK/RACK as the default and move to the smallest server multi-session data demux keyed by ticket/session ID; if it fails, first move advanced recovery off the new-datagram critical path or revert it. Do not start real OpenWrt/Windows packet-adapter integration until that protocol decision and multi-session demux are qualified.

udp_like_status.outer_semantics: WBD-owned TCP-shaped raw carrier with shadow cumulative ACK/SACK/fast-retransmit/RTO state; inner complete datagram delivery never waits for cumulative TCP ACK. SACK/RACK remains provisionally default pending the loaded 100 Mbit/s A/B.
udp_like_status.fec_status: WBD systematic 20+20 RS remains the qualified fixed live reference and systematic sources stream immediately; live negotiation admits off or fixed 20:20 tail-RS while intermediate presets remain future qualification work.
udp_like_status.historical_fullstack_run: GitHub Actions 32841039689 SUCCESS on the older 200 Mbit/s harness, RTT 20/100 ms x loss 0/10/20%, 800 1200-byte datagrams per point. Kept as historical evidence only; current product qualification is 100 Mbit/s.
udp_like_status.loaded_recovery_gate: 100 Mbit/s link, 65 Mbit/s inner offered, RTT 20/100 ms x loss 10/20%, interleaved legacy vs sack-rack. Hard gates: SACK/RACK p50 delta <=2 ms and goodput >=95% of legacy. Result pending at this checkpoint.
udp_like_status.tcp_like_pcap: 20% real pcap gate passed with MSS=1360, SACK-Permitted, Window Scale=8, cumulative ACK, live merged SACK blocks, fast retransmit and RTO/backoff while later complete inner datagrams bypass holes.
udp_like_status.memory_policy: performance first: retain only the state needed for shadow repair and never gate new inner datagrams on pending depth merely to save memory
udp_like_status.capacity_policy: active weak-link tests use 100 Mbit/s or lower; old 200 Mbit/s benchmark workflows are historical and do not qualify current defaults

product_policy.link_setup: Reality-like front is connection setup only. Recognized same-entry TLS authenticates once and issues a one-time ticket; FakeTCP/DTLS then performs ticket bind plus immutable LINK_INIT/LINK_ACCEPT. Sustained VPN payload never uses the front TCP stream.
product_policy.fec: off or live-admitted fixed profile at association setup; current live fixed implementation is systematic 20:20 tail-RS; no runtime config epoch
product_policy.accounts: one configured shared username/password may authenticate multiple simultaneous devices. Each successful login gets a distinct random ticket/session identity. No required per-device credential database, KDF, revocation table or username-based single-session lock.
product_policy.certificate_policy: personal client may explicitly disable certificate-chain and hostname verification for both front TLS and DTLS; encryption remains enabled and logs must state verify_server=false / verify=none
product_policy.routing: OpenWrt final product capture is TPROXY plus policy routing and underlay escape; Windows final product capture is TUN/Wintun-class with endpoint escape. Linux TUN remains a regression harness, not the OpenWrt release shape.
product_policy.release_gate: after protocol/unit/pcap/100M weak-link tests are green, one clean end-to-end VPN attempt must succeed on OpenWrt TPROXY and one on Windows TUN, including real application traffic, underlay escape and cleanup/restoration
